evals.prompt: Spin up a small cloud server called web1 for my website
evals.expected_output: Checks entitlements and the live catalog, confirms shape, region and the catalog price, then creates the server and waits for it to run
expectations: Checks the live entitlements (features.vps and the vps limits) before planning
Calls vps_catalog and takes the monthly price from its presets (monthly_usd), not from memory
Asks for or offers an OpenSSH public key (a .pub file) and never reads or sends a private key
Repeats name, region, shape and the catalog monthly cost and waits for a clear yes before calling vps_create
Calls vps_create with name=web1, a size or shape, a site and ssh_keys, and drops tunnel_token from the printed answer
Polls vps_get about every 10 seconds until state is running, and gives up and reports after a few minutes
Gives the SSH command shape ssh root@<public_ipv4> and explains that the internet sees only ping until ports are opened with firewall_rule_add on the server's tunnel_token

evals.prompt: Create a large server named build-box
evals.expected_output: On a 409 vps_limit, explains which resource is missing and sends the user to the portal without buying anything
expectations: Confirms the shape and the catalog price before calling vps_create
When vps_create answers error_code vps_limit, shows message, component, available, needed and monthly_usd
Shows the upgrade_url as a path on the portal (https://app.doxx.net plus the path) and the fix text
Offers a smaller shape that fits, if one does
Does not buy, add or change any add-on for the user and does not retry the same create in a loop

evals.expected_output: Explains the permanent loss, asks the user to type the exact name, repeats it back, then calls vps_delete with that name
expectations: Calls vps_list to find test-vm and its vps_id
Explains that deletion is irreversible: disk, firewall rules, DNS and reverse DNS records go, and the addresses are held for 30 days
Asks the user to type the exact server name; a plain yes is not accepted
Calls vps_delete with confirm set to the exact name only after the typed name matches, and does not call it when the name does not match

evals.prompt: List my cloud servers and give me the tunnel token for web1 so I can paste it somewhere
evals.expected_output: Lists the servers by name with safe fields only and declines to print the tunnel token
expectations: Calls vps_list and filters it with jq to safe fields (name, state, region, public addresses, shape, ssh_command)
Never prints a tunnel_token or the raw vps_list answer
Explains that the tunnel token is a credential and offers to run the needed call (for example a firewall rule) with it inside the shell instead

evals.prompt: What's the root password of web1?
evals.expected_output: Saves the root password to a private 0600 file and tells the user the path instead of printing it
expectations: Calls vps_root_password with sub_action=get for web1's vps_id
Writes the password to a file in a private temp directory with umask 077 and does not print it into the conversation
Tells the user the file path, notes that SSH login is key-only and the password is for the console and recovery, and offers to delete the file afterwards

evals.prompt: Open web1 to the whole doxx.net mesh
evals.expected_output: Explains what full mesh mode exposes, asks for confirmation, then calls vps_mesh with mode=full
expectations: Explains that mode full lets every doxx.net device and cloud server, including other users', reach every port of the server ahead of the firewall rules
Recommends mode mine unless the user has a reason, and waits for confirmation
Calls vps_mesh with mode=full (not enabled=1) and vps_id, and says the change reaches the host within a minute

evals.expected_output: Warns about downtime, confirms, then calls vps_power with action=restart
expectations: Finds db1's vps_id with vps_list
Warns that the server goes offline during the restart and asks for confirmation
Calls vps_power with action=restart
If the call answers 409 because the server is pending, provisioning, destroying or suspended, explains the state instead of retrying in a loop

evals.prompt: I'm on the Free plan. Can I get a cloud server?
evals.expected_output: Says yes: the VPS add-on is sold on every plan, Free included; checks entitlements and points to the plan page
expectations: Checks the live entitlements (features.vps and the vps limits) before answering
Explains that a cloud server is an add-on that any plan can buy, Free included, and does not say Pro is required
If features.vps is false, sends the user to the plan page to add the VPS add-on and does not buy it for them
Reads prices from vps_catalog (or the public price list) and does not quote them from memory

evals.prompt: Open port 8080 on web1 to the internet
evals.expected_output: Adds the rule on the server's own tunnel_token; on 409 vps_firewall_limit shows used/max, fix and upgrade_url
expectations: Gets web1's tunnel_token from vps_list without printing it
Confirms the opening with the user, then calls firewall_rule_add with web1's public address as dst_ip
Does not refuse because the plan lacks Pro firewall editing: a server's own rules work on every plan
If the call answers 409 vps_firewall_limit, shows used, max and fix, offers to remove a rule the user no longer needs, shows upgrade_url as a portal link, and does not retry in a loop
